algorithm.title: Diagnostic Algorithm for Approaching the Patient with Ankylosing Spondylitis.

cell.label: 4 of 5 of the following: (1) onset of back discomfort before the age of 40 years, (2) insidious onset, (3) persistence for at least 3 months, (4) associated with morning stiffness, or (5) improvement with exercise?
25% probability of having AS assuming 5% prevalence of AS in chronic low back pain.
Anterior spine flexion of <5 cm (Schober's test) and chest expansion of <2.5 cm increase probability of diagnosis but are often absent in early disease.
Order sacroiliac x-ray. Is the radiologic criterion of grade 2 sacroiilitis bilaterally or grade 3 or 4 unilaterally satisfied?
Patient still has possible early AS. Order HLA-B27.
Patient has a 80% chance of having early AS. Consider a trial of NSAIDs and physical therapy or a rheumatologist referral.
Patient has less than 3% chance of having AS. Consider another diagnosis.

footnotes.footnote: Data from van der Linden S, Valkenburg HA, Cats A. Evaluation of diagnostic criteria for ankylosing spondylitis. A proposal for modification of the New York criteria. Arthritis Rheum 1984;27:361-368. and Rudwaleit M, Metter A, Listing J, Sieper J, Braun J. Inflammatory back pain in ankylosing spondylitis: a reassessment of the clinical history for application as classification and diagnostic criteria. Arthritis Rheum 2006;54:569-578.
